claims.statement: For a bounded full-rank chart A_B=B V^T with known V in R^{q x r}, if an adaptive sensing algorithm receives m responses from alphabets of size at most 2^b and must answer all post-storage bilinear tasks (a,x) uniformly to error epsilon with failure probability delta, then for p>=q and epsilon<=1/(64 sqrt(r)), mb >= (1-delta)pr log2(1/(32 sqrt(r) epsilon))-h2(delta); transpose the construction for q>p. The lower bound is information-theoretic and permits unbounded computation.
assumptions: rank(A_B)=r; B lies in an operator-norm ball of radius 1/(8 sqrt(r)) around (1/(2 sqrt(r)))[I_r;0] when p>=q
measurement queries are adaptive scalar linear functionals of A; each response has at most b bits
all algorithm randomness is independent of A and included in the retained state
after storage, the decoder simultaneously answers every unit bilinear task a^T A x to epsilon with failure probability delta<1/2
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; proof in PROOF.md; external correctness, novelty and priority unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Adjacent generic exact low-rank recovery and adaptive noisy matrix-recovery results are established prior art. This task-specific finite-bit post-storage bilinear query interface is not claimed novel; priority needs literature/expert review.
claims.costs: Lower counts m calls and b response bits per call; omits query encoding, calibration, physical noise/SNR, and computation. Raw coordinate baseline uses pr calls, b_raw=ceil(log2(4 sqrt(pr)/epsilon)) response bits per call, O(pr) quantization operations, and O(pr+qr) decoder arithmetic.
claims.falsifier: Find a protocol under the stated oracle, task, and uniform error interface that answers all bilinear tasks while using fewer response bits than the packing/Fano bound, or identify a flaw in the operator-norm packing reduction.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review, then investigate whether a restricted low-entropy task distribution yields a positive acquisition-vs-raw-data result under an equally informed baseline.

claims.statement: For a deterministic adaptive exact-real linear measurement scheme on the same p x r open chart, fewer than pr scalar queries leave locally indistinguishable rank-r factors, so uniform post-storage bilinear accuracy epsilon<R/2 is impossible.
assumptions: p>=q and known V has orthonormal columns
unknown B varies over an open operator-norm ball of radius R=1/(8 sqrt(r)) around a full-rank center
queries are exact scalar linear functionals and are deterministic adaptive functions of prior responses
decoder must answer all unit bilinear tasks uniformly
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; deterministic scope only; external review and novelty unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a local dimension/nullspace obstruction adjacent to classical low-rank measurement-count bounds; not claimed as a new general recovery theorem.
claims.costs: Counts scalar exact-real measurement calls; exact precision is an idealized generous interface. Randomized positive-error query-count version not established.
claims.falsifier: Construct a deterministic adaptive scheme with fewer than pr exact scalar linear queries that uniformly answers every bilinear task on the open rank-r chart to epsilon<R/2.
claims.next_gate: Do not extend to randomized positive-error schemes without a separate minimax proof.
